The Petitioner is a wholly owned subsidiary of SJVN Limited (“SJVNL”), (a joint venture of the Government of India and the Government of Himachal Pradesh), incorporated for execution of a 1320 MW (2x660 MW) project in Chausa, District Buxar, Bihar. The Petitioner's holding company, SJVNL, took over Buxar Bijlee Company Pvt. Limited from the Govt. of Bihar and renamed it SJVN Thermal (P) Limited (“STPL”) (the Petitioner company). 3. The Petitioner has submitted the impugned petition seeking determination of tariff for the period from 14.11.2025 (COD of Unit-1) to 31.3.2029 in respect of the BTPP. The Petitioner has also prayed for interim tariff pending final determination of tariff in accordance with Regulations 9 and 10(3) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. 4. The Petitioner has submitted that erstwhile Bihar State Electricity Board, now Bihar State Power (Holding) Company Limited (BSPHCL), entered into a PPA dated 5.1.2011 with Buxar Bijli Company Private Limited for setting up BTPP at Chausa in Buxar District, Bihar. SJVN Limited took over the said PPA and subsequently assigned it to NBPDCL vide resolution dated 1.6.2018. Subsequently, a supplementary PPA was also executed among SJVN, BSPHCL and the Bihar distribution companies on 9.4.2021. 6. The Petitioner has further submitted that the Eastern Regional Power Committee (ERPC) proposed a tentative distribution of the unallocated power among Bihar, West Bengal, Jharkhand, Odisha and Sikkim on 6.6.2025, which could not fructify. Accordingly, the Petitioner was advised to approach MoP/Central Electricity Authority for further directions. Pending finalisation of long-term arrangements, the Petitioner explored sale of power to DVC, Indian Railways, GUVNL, KSEB Ltd and TNPDCL and entered into a PPA dated 31.12.2025 with its holding company, SJVN, for sale of unallocated or un-requisitioned power through the Power Exchange or bilateral market, subject to mutually agreed terms, availability of transmission corridor and applicable market conditions. 7. The Petitioner has filed this petition in accordance with Regulation 9(1) and 10 of the 2024 Tariff Regulations, after serving a copy of the same on the Respondents. Accordingly, the annual fixed charges claimed by the Petitioner are as under: 10. The Petitioner, in compliance of the above direction, has submitted that the RCE of BTPP amounting to Rs. 13,756.56 crore (inclusive of taxes) has been approved by the 105 th meeting of the Board of Directors of the Petitioner company on 31.7.2025, which has subsequently also approved by the Board of Directors of SJVN Limited (the holding company) on 10.11.2025, along with the approval for infusion of additional equity in the Project and approval for onwards submission to the MoP for further approval of Cabinet/ CCEA. The Petitioner has further submitted that a letter dated 12.12.2025 was sent to MoP for consideration of the RCE of Rs. 13,756.56 crore at the November, 2024 Price Level, and onward submission to the CCEA for approval, which is presently under consideration. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that at the time of filing the Petition, commissioning of Unit-II was anticipated, and had accordingly filed tariff forms for both the units and requested one week’s time to file revised tariff forms in respect of Unit-I, being the commissioned unit. The Petitioner has further submitted that the trial run of Unit-II is underway and that the same is expected to be commissioned in August 2026. The learned counsel for the Respondent, BSPHCL, submitted that the Petition and the tariff forms on record were incomplete, did not comply 15. We have considered the submissions made by the parties. The Petitioner has submitted that the commissioning of Unit-I encountered time overruns on account of factors beyond the reasonable control of the Petitioner, including delays in land acquisition for railway siding, water corridor, statutory clearances, and other extraneous circumstances. 27.
